logistic-model.def: A differential equation in which the rate of change is jointly proportional to the quantity and to the room left below a limit $K$: $\frac{dP}{dt} = kP(K - P)$, or $rP\left(1 - \frac{P}{K}\right)$. Positive solutions approach $K$, and growth is fastest at $P = \frac{K}{2}$.

carrying-capacity.def: In a logistic model, the positive value $K$ at which the rate of change is 0; for any positive starting value, $\lim_{t \to \infty} P(t) = K$. Read it from $\frac{dP}{dt} = kP(K - P)$ by setting the rate to 0.
